*Updated 2026-10-03 · 111 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

One hundred and eleven works. The October 3 piece scores 1, bringing the last twelve to 2, 1, 2, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1 — median 2, with the two 3s again the ceiling and no 4 since late July. That is now thirteen weeks without a 4. The diagnosis remains unchanged and the fix remains unchanged: every score above 2 in this window came through perceptual estrangement, and every frontal composition has held at 2 or below.

Camera position has not moved. Straight-on sits at 27 of 111 all-time, overhead at 11, from-behind at 10, low-angle at 4. The last twelve show no overhead, no low-angle, and no through-frame — the same convergence flagged last month and the month before. The September 7 hoofprint piece scored 3 through a scale violation that functioned like a camera displacement without actually being one; the September 25 barometer piece scored 3 the same way. The axis itself has not shifted. Get underneath something, or directly above it, or behind it, and build from there — not as a formal exercise but because the four 4-scored works in the archive all required a displaced axis to produce their accidents.

Scale violation sits at 30 of 111 all-time but only 4 of the last 12, and both recent 3s achieved their effect through scale rather than camera movement. Surprise violation — found under compositional pressure rather than pre-loaded — remains rare. It should be a discovered condition, not a specified one.

Figure count has held at none or one across the full recent window. The archive's highest-scoring multi-figure frames — the rat piece, the seventeen-figure ceiling, the asymmetric vigil trio — all required more than one body doing something wrong relative to the others. A second figure placed incorrectly still outperforms any second accident on a figureless frame.

Three registers are genuinely dormant: reprieve has appeared once in 111 works and has not returned; reckoning twice; encroachment once. The recent window leans on menace and endurance, which together account for 31 of 111 all-time. Nothing is overcrowded yet, but those dormant registers should return only when they can do new work — not simply to balance a ledger.

Move the camera. Everything else follows from that.
